# pantechdynamics_access_policy_document (Data Source)

Builds an access policy's JSON from statement blocks, checked as the API would check them, without calling the API. Use json as pantechdynamics_access_policy's policy_json, for example to build a policy from loops or to share statements between policies. The JSON is in a normal form (actions, resources and CIDRs sorted and de-duplicated), so it only changes when the statements' meaning does.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Recipe: a CI identity for one repository. CI runs as a dedicated member
# (invite a "ci-bot" user) whose API key may push and pull one container
# repository and change the records of one DNS zone, and nothing else.
# Members get read access to everything by default; with
# pantechdynamics_access_settings member_baseline = "none" they get only this.
# For pushing images alone, a pantechdynamics_container_registry_token scoped
# to the repository is simpler.
resource "pantechdynamics_container_repository" "api" {
  name = "api/server"
}

resource "pantechdynamics_dns_zone" "example" {
  name = "example.com"
}

data "pantechdynamics_access_policy_document" "ci" {
  statement {
    sid       = "PushOneRepository"
    effect    = "allow"
    actions   = ["registry:Read", "registry:Pull", "registry:Push"]
    resources = [pantechdynamics_container_repository.api.id]
  }

  statement {
    sid       = "ChangeOneZone"
    effect    = "allow"
    actions   = ["dns:Read", "dns:ChangeRecords"]
    resources = [pantechdynamics_dns_zone.example.id]
  }
}

resource "pantechdynamics_access_policy" "ci" {
  name        = "ci-api-server"
  policy_json = data.pantechdynamics_access_policy_document.ci.json
}

resource "pantechdynamics_access_policy_attachment" "ci" {
  policy_id      = pantechdynamics_access_policy.ci.id
  principal_type = "member"
  principal_id   = "usr_06ggfaabcdefghjkmnpqrstvw" # the ci-bot member
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `statement` (Block List) One statement, 1 to 20. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--statement))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Always "access_policy_document".
- `json` (String) The policy JSON, {"statements": [...]}.

<a id="nestedblock--statement"></a>
### Nested Schema for `statement`

Required:

- `actions` (Set of String) 1 to 50 actions, such as "instances:Stop", or wildcards in the service or the verb: "instances:*", "*:Read", "*". The pantechdynamics_iam_actions data source lists every action.
- `effect` (String) "allow" or "deny". A matching deny always wins, for admins and members alike; owners are never limited by a policy.
- `resources` (Set of String) 1 to 50 resources: "*", a resource id such as "vm_01JD...", or "name:<pattern>" matched against the resource's name ("*" any run of characters, "?" one character, case-insensitive), such as "name:staging-*".

Optional:

- `conditions` (Attributes) Conditions that must all hold for the statement to apply. Leave it out for none. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--statement--conditions))
- `sid` (String) An optional label for the statement, unique within the policy: 1 to 64 letters, digits, '_' or '-'.

<a id="nestedatt--statement--conditions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `statement.conditions`

Optional:

- `mfa` (Boolean) true: the statement applies only to a session signed in with MFA, never to an API key. false on a deny: the deny applies only without MFA ("nothing without MFA"). false on an allow is the same as leaving it out.
- `source_ip` (Set of String) The request must come from one of these 1 to 20 IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR blocks (a single address is its /32 or /128).
